principles: Only fix real consumption and lifecycle gaps, not arbitrary automation.
Historical backfill creates inert candidate material only; activation remains evidence-gated.
All new surfaces remain host-neutral and non-authoritative.
Digest-bound dry-run/apply contracts are required for large batch mutations.
Timer automation must be explicit, bounded, observable, and safe to rerun.
drivers: 2074 currently proposable historical seeds are not practical to process through manual small-batch loops.
Candidate playbooks currently have no exposure/outcome path, so promotion cannot progress from real evidence.
The user explicitly wants future-work items completed without weakening Proofbound evidence boundaries.

options.name: single_explicit_cli_closure
pros: Keeps all actions auditable and manually invocable while still eliminating repetitive loops
Reuses existing seed/proposal/candidate and auto-promotion guards
Avoids hidden background mutation and preserves host-neutral CLI boundaries
cons: Requires users or a scheduler to invoke the timer command
Still cannot activate candidates without real outcomes

options.name: hidden_background_daemon
pros: Would require less manual invocation once installed
cons: Can surprise users with background mutations
Risks violating the no hidden daemon scope boundary

options.name: activate_from_backfill
pros: Would quickly turn historical experience into runtime guidance
cons: Unsafe because historical seed existence is not proof the playbook helped
Would contradict DONE success alone cannot count as helped

rationale: The explicit CLI closure solves the real throughput and learning-consumption gaps while preserving Proofbound evidence boundaries: large backfill is digest-bound and inert, trial records exposure evidence, and timer automation only runs bounded safe actions.

preMortem.scenario: Backfill creates duplicate or active playbooks
preMortem.trigger: Apply reuses stale observe data or ignores represented canonical keys
preMortem.consequence: Learning store grows misleading duplicate runtime material
preMortem.mitigation: Require observe digest, recompute representation before candidate write, and assert all created rows are status=candidate.

preMortem.scenario: Trial exposure is mistaken for helped outcome
preMortem.trigger: Trial command writes helped verdicts automatically
preMortem.mitigation: Trial writes exposure/control observations only; helped still requires explicit playbook_outcome_record or equivalent structured outcome.

preMortem.scenario: Timer becomes an unsafe hidden daemon
preMortem.trigger: Timer registers or runs unbounded background mutation by default
preMortem.consequence: Users cannot audit when learning state changes
preMortem.mitigation: Implement an explicit command with dry-run default, apply flag, per-action flags, and bounded limits.

preMortem.scenario: Promotion sweep or activation runs without feature policy
preMortem.trigger: Timer calls apply paths without existing feature/evidence guards
preMortem.mitigation: Timer delegates to existing guarded apply reports and reports blockers instead of bypassing them.
